data: Do the distributions of distances between non-related pairs and related pairs on Twitter data have the same peak?

The caption states that the figure shows example distributions of distances between non-related pairs (light grey) and related pairs (dark grey) on Twitter data, using a simple mean of word embeddings. The question asks whether the distributions of distances between non-related pairs and related pairs have the same peak. From the analysis of the figure, the two distributions appear to have similar peaks, with both distributions showing a peak at approximately the same normalized distance value. Therefore, the answer is yes, the distributions of distances between non-related pairs and related pairs on Twitter data have the same peak.
